Lessons.Title: Negative Rational Exponents
ExplanationParagraphs: Source-aligned goals: Draw a graph representing negative rational exponents and use it to estimate values. Use both radicals and exponents to represent numbers.
For b>0, b^(-m/n)=1/b^(m/n); negative exponent takes a reciprocal, not a negative number.

Source activity 5.1: Math Talk: Don’t Be Negative: \(9^{\text-\frac12}\) Explain the mathematical model, verify the relevant result and have a teacher inspect original diagrams or discussion evidence.

Source activity 5.2: Negative Fractional Powers Are Just Numbers: Complete the table as much as you can without using a calculator. (You should be able to fill in three spaces.) Plot these powers of 2 in the coordinate plane. ​​​​​​ Connect the points as smoothly as you can. Use your graph of \(y=2^x\) to estimate the value of the other powers in the table, and write your estimates in the table. Let’s investigate \(2^{\text{-} \frac13}\).… Explain the mathematical model, verify the relevant result and have a teacher inspect original diagrams or discussion evidence.

Source activity 5.3: Any Fraction Can Be an Exponent: \(8^{\frac45}\), \(\sqrt[4]{8}^5\), \(\sqrt[5]{8}^4\) \(8^{\text{-} \frac45}\), \(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt[5]{8^4}}\), \(\text-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt[5]{8^4}}\) \(\sqrt{4^3}\), \(4^{\frac32}\), \(4^{\frac23}\) \(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{4^3}}\), \(\text-4^{\frac32}\), \(4^{\text-\frac32}\) For each set of 3 numbers, cross out the expression that is not equal to the other two expressions.… Explain the mathematical model, verify the relevant result and have a teacher inspect original diagrams or discussion evidence.

Source activity 5.4: Make These Exponents Less Complicated: Match expressions into groups according to whether they are equal. Be prepared to explain your reasoning. \(\left(\sqrt{3}\right)^4\) \(\left (3^{\frac12}\right )^4\) \((\sqrt{3})^2 \boldcdot (\sqrt{3})^2\) \(\left (3^2 \right) ^{\frac12}\) \(\left (3^{\frac12}\right)^2\) When we have a number with a negative exponent, it just means we need to find the reciprocal of the number… Explain the mathematical model, verify the relevant result and have a teacher inspect original diagrams or discussion evidence.

Practice Problem 1: Write each expression in the form \(a^b\), without using any radicals. \(\frac{1}{\sqrt[3]{12}}\) Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.
Practice Problem 2: Write \(32^{\text-\frac25}\) without using exponents or radicals. Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.
Practice Problem 3: Match the equivalent expressions. \(8^{\text- \frac13}\) \(16^{\text- \frac{1}{2}}\) Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 4: Complete the table. Use powers of 27 in the top row and radicals or rational numbers in the bottom row. Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.
Practice Problem 5: What are the solutions to the equation \((x-1)(x+2)=\text-2\)? Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.
Practice Problem 6: Use exponent rules to explain why \((\sqrt{5})^3 = \sqrt{5^3}\). Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.
Edulytics independent cool-down: Evaluate 27^(-2/3). Expected reasoning or answer: 1/9.
